svg.title: The flight loop as wm-flight-wiring.edn declares it
svg.text: The flight loop as the wiring map declares it
Generated from holes/labs/M-wm-wiring/wm-flight-wiring.edn (47513216, futon3c HEAD 29df1244) by spike/wm_wiring_svg.bb; not hand edited. 100 boxes, 73 fields.
Each panel is one step of the flight, in order. A box is a source var the map pins, listing what it writes (w) and reads (r). A field kept inside a step is an arrow inside its panel.

A field that crosses steps is one line in the band below, tapped by its writer (dot) and each reader (arrow). The registered test checks each site at the pins (futon2 663caa7b, futon3c 58f1a8cb), expecting 281 findings (4 to-do). 20 fields cross steps; 0 of 11 steps are entered or left by none.

Hand-off strip: between two steps, how many declared fields cross that boundary in the flight's direction (a purple line below is a field crossing the other way).

svg.text: solid box: built component at its pinned var (76)
dashed amber box: declared, not built, drawn at its intended site (1)
dotted box: the step's registered test, a declared reader; it lists its reads and draws no arrows (23)
grey box: siteless component, exempt from conformance (3)
line: a field, from its one writer to its readers, both built (65 reader arrows; 20 fields cross steps, 42 stay inside one)
dashed amber: declared on a box not yet built (6)
purple: the reader is an earlier step than the writer, the loop closing (5)
grey stub: a field read that no box writes (13); green stub: the owner's text, exogenous (1)

Numbered rings: the exemplar trace the map records for M-autoclock-in, in order (loop-entry > r1-outer-cascade > flight-entry > dispatch > clock-in > r2-served-by-reading > r2-verifier > r6-cascade-lane > r9-selection-law > r0-enact-step > r7-flight-call > wc-checker > r7-increment > r7-fold > r1-outer-cascade). Boxes on it have a heavier border.

What this does not show: the prover reads sites textually, so a field's presence at a var is what is checked, not that the value flows; the eleven code shapes it cannot see are listed in WM-MAP-REPLAY-D. Standing findings (277) are generic keys the prover cannot scope per box.

A red chevron in the hand-off strip is a boundary no declared field crosses in the flight's direction; the code hands data across it through the flight record and the store's published view, which no box carries yet.
A step marked as entered or left by no field is one whose inputs and outputs the map does not yet declare; that is a gap in the map, not in the drawing.
Organisation: who calls whom, in order (from the source, at futon2 3fcfa0df)

Each box once, under its first caller in flight order; siblings in body order (numbered). 71 placed, 102 calls (83 direct, 8 hand-off invocations, 3 hand-checked cross-process, 8 closure constructions), 70 with a condition (printed on the edge). 33 callers placed elsewhere are thin grey arcs.

Generated by spike/wm_org_layer.bb at map 47513216 (wm-org-layer.edn); its three hand-checked edges' evidence sites are re-verified on every run. Lanes derived from this order disagree with the panels' hand-kept lane table for 11 boxes (listed at the foot).
hand-off: a closure the caller was handed, invoked
builds a closure another box invokes

g.title: clock-in — futon3c/src/futon3c/agency/clock_lineage.clj persist-clock! full_loop_runner/dispatch! POSTs /api/alpha/bell with :mission-id (cross-JVM HTTP); in futon3c, agency/clock_decision.clj:293 calls clock_lineage/persist-clock!. The hop from the bell to the clock decision is not traced here: this edge is the map's :traces hop, not a read of the path

click-start — futon3c/src/futon3c/transport/http.clj handle-wm-click-start http-click-fn POSTs /api/alpha/wm/click (flight_runner.clj:495-511, cross-JVM HTTP); futon3c transport/http.clj:9295 routes the POST to handle-wm-click-start

wc-checker siteless (futon3c holes/labs/M-futon-seams/exemplar/proof2a_check.clj); wc-verdict-fn runs it as a bb subprocess (flight_runner.clj:915-922, :checker opt; the map's :traces hop r7-flight-call -> wc-checker)
